statement_fidelity.note: Marked metadata statement_status=consistent; mathematical inputs unchanged. Read task source FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/12.lean at pinned commit, full IsGood and target. erdosproblems.com/12 (saved problem-web.html/txt) explicitly states arbitrary f→∞, same no-distinct-triple property, strict cardinality>N/f(N) infinitely often. Erdos–Sarkozy, Proc. London Math. Soc.21(1970)97–101, p98 (https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1970-13.pdf; extracted erdos-source-extracted.md) constructs such sets using factorial congruence blocks. Paper wording assumes increasing f; arbitrary divergent natural f admits a divergent nondecreasing minorant, so task is a valid variant. f may vanish only at finitely many large-range exceptions; real division, positive interval [1,N], strict bound, infinite A and infinitely-many N all consistent. It does not claim the open reciprocal-sum part or density-zero theorem is proved.
